text: For Paul, the stage entrance of that theater was the actual portal of Romance, and once he passed through it, the dull world of Cordelia Street simply ceased to exist. <break time="0.8s" /> He did not want to become an actor, any more than he wanted to become a musician, for what he wanted was to be carried away from everything. <break time="0.8s" /> After a night behind the scenes, Paul found the schoolroom more repulsive than ever, with its bare floors and naked walls and prosy teachers who never wore violets in their buttonholes. <break time="0.8s" /> To make up for this, he told his classmates wild stories about his friendship with the actors, boasting that he would soon leave school to sail for Naples, Venice, and Egypt. <break time="0.8s" /> When his teachers complained once again, the principal went to Pauls father, and it was decided that the boy must be taken out of school and put to work. <break time="0.8s" /> Another usher was found to take his place at the hall, the theater doorkeeper was warned not to admit him, and Charley Edwards remorsefully promised never to see him again. <break time="0.8s" /> Paul was sent to work as an office boy for Denny and Carson, and it was there, on a Friday afternoon, that he was given the firms money to deposit in the bank. <break time="0.8s" /> Instead of taking it to the bank, he kept the money and boarded a train for the East, and the next gray dawn found him rushing through a January snowstorm toward New York.
